req.title: Reject wrong method on /post
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than POST on /post.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /post must return HTTP 405 for any method other than POST. Tests cover: (1) positive path — POST returns 200 with expected JSON keys; (2) negative paths — GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE each return exactly 405; (3) boundary — HEAD and OPTIONS (edge-case methods) also return 405. Each assertion uses exact status codes to catch comparison-operator mutations (== vs >=, 405 vs 404, etc.). The positive test also asserts response body structure to catch mutations that alter the handler's return value.

tests.name: test_post_method_returns_200_with_expected_payload
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send HTTP POST to /post with form data
expected: Response JSON contains keys: url, args, form, data, origin, headers, files, json
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005 positive: POST is the only allowed method; it must succeed with 200
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_method_returns_200_with_expected_payload():
    r = client.post('/post', data={'key': 'value'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body is not None
    for key in ('url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json'):
        assert key in body, f'Missing key: {key}'
    assert body['form'] == {'key': 'value'}

test_post_method_returns_200_with_expected_payload()

tests.name: test_head_on_post_endpoint_returns_405_or_200_boundary
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
HEAD is an edge-case method not listed in the route's methods tuple
actions: Assert status code is NOT 200 (HEAD should not succeed as POST)
expected: HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed (Flask does not auto-allow HEAD for POST-only routes)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005 BVA boundary: HEAD is adjacent to GET in HTTP method space; Flask only auto-adds HEAD for GET routes, not POST-only routes
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_head_on_post_endpoint_returns_405_boundary():
    r = client.head('/post')
    assert r.status_code == 405
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 200

test_head_on_post_endpoint_returns_405_boundary()

tests.name: test_post_status_code_is_exactly_200_not_201_or_204
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send HTTP POST to /post with JSON body
Assert status code is exactly 200, not 201 or 204
expected: Response JSON body key 'json' contains the posted JSON object
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005 BVA: status code boundary — 200 is correct, 201/204 would be wrong; catches constant-mutation on status code
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_status_code_is_exactly_200_not_201_or_204():
    payload = json.dumps({'answer': 42})
    r = client.post(
        '/post',
        data=payload,
        content_type='application/json'
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.status_code != 201
    assert r.status_code != 204
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body is not None
    assert body['json'] == {'answer': 42}

test_post_status_code_is_exactly_200_not_201_or_204()

tests.name: test_wrong_method_status_code_is_exactly_405_not_404_or_400
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Assert status code is exactly 405, not 404 or 400
expected: HTTP 405 exactly — not 404 Not Found, not 400 Bad Request
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005 NEG + constant-mutation: 405 is the required error code; catches mutations to 404, 400, or 200
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_wrong_method_status_code_is_exactly_405_not_404_or_400():
    r = client.get('/post')
    assert r.status_code == 405
    assert r.status_code != 404
    assert r.status_code != 400
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 500

test_wrong_method_status_code_is_exactly_405_not_404_or_400()
